Here there is a need for you to follow me, not I you. And although you may still thunder many things against me, my Monarchy shall nevertheless stand, while all of yours goes to ruin. It is not in vain that I write so extensively about Alchemy, but I do it with this mind and purpose: that from these things you may nearly and solidly recognize what lies hidden within it, and how it ought to be understood. Nor should you be offended by this: that neither gold nor silver comes forth from it. But rather, care must be taken that through it <term>arcana</term> <gloss>hidden healing secrets</gloss> are uncovered, and the deceptions of the <term>seplasiarii</term> <gloss>perfumers or ointment-sellers</gloss> are exposed, by which the unrefined common people are deceived, while these men provide for one <term>floren</term> <gloss>gold coin</gloss> what they would not redeem for a single penny. So "precious" are their secrets.

### ON ALCHEMY.

<margin>The end of Alchemy is not gold and silver, but arcana.</margin>
<margin>Poison even in the best things.</margin>
Who is there who would dare to deny that poison lies hidden and exists even in the best of things? All are compelled to confess this. Therefore, if this is true, I now ask of you: must not the poison be separated from the good and useful? And the good be accepted, the evil left behind? Indeed, so it must be. If it is necessary, then, I pray, tell me how that is separated in your workshops? For among you, all things remain mixed together. But so that you may protect your simplicity, if you are convicted into confessing that poison lies hidden there, and are asked where it finally goes: then you bring forth I know not what concerning "corrections" which might drive out and remove the poison, 
<margin>The correction of the Physicians is examined.</margin>
just as they say Quince corrects Scammony, or later <term>Diagridium</term> <gloss>a preparation of scammony juice</gloss>. But what kind of correction is that? Does not the poison remain afterward just as at first? And yet you meanwhile boast that you have corrected it, so much so that the poison no longer harms. But where did it escape to? 
<margin>Diagridion.</margin>
It remains in the <term>Diagridium</term>. Try it, if you are wise: exceed the limit, and you will see where the poison is. For you will know it quickly enough. Thus you also correct <term>Turbith</term> <gloss>the root of a purgative plant</gloss> and call it <term>Diaturbith</term>. Your corrections are of such a kind that they would be fit for peasants and should be given to pack-horses. Make the danger by exceeding the limit and increase the dose: you will see if you do not feel the poison. 
<margin>What it is to correct, Physician.</margin>
*To correct is to take up that which has been corrected.* If one who is malicious and has sinned is punished, the correction does not extend further than the will of the one who was punished lasts. Such are these corrections of yours; the state remains with the things themselves, not with you. Now indeed, in this case, a Physician must consider nothing more than that the poison be taken away. This must be done through separation. As for example: a serpent is poisonous, and yet it is adopted for food. If you take away the poison from it, you may eat with no harm. The same is to be understood equally concerning all other things, namely that there is need for a similar separation. Until that is done, you cannot be secure in your operation, unless by chance it happens that nature supplies your deficiencies, or a greater kindness of the heavens favors you. For in your art, no protection will have remained.

Now therefore, at last, if that true foundation is necessary which removes the poison, consider how Alchemy performs it. For this must be done in such a way that, if <term>Mars</term> <gloss>Iron</gloss> be in the <term>Sun</term> <gloss>Gold</gloss>, Mars is taken away; and if <term>Saturn</term> <gloss>Lead</gloss> dwells in <term>Venus</term> <gloss>Copper</gloss>, it is separated from her. For as many ascendants and impressions as there are in the things of nature, so many bodies also exist in them. But as for those bodies which are contrary, it is entirely necessary that some of them be taken away and removed, so that in this way all contrariety is lifted, and the evil which you seek to remove is taken from the good. 
<margin>Fire perfects all things.</margin>
As gold is useful for nothing unless it is first cast into the fire, so a Medicine is much less useful which does not pass through the fire. For it is necessary for all things to pass through the fire into a second generation, by which it ought to benefit and help man. And should this not deservedly be judged the upright foundation of any Physician? For a Physician ought to apply not poisons, but <term>arcana</term>. 
<margin>Workshops rebuked.</margin>
However, all those preparations of the <term>officinae</term> <gloss>apothecary shops</gloss>, as many as there are, do not contribute even a small letter to this doctrine; but they are occupied simply in "correcting." It is as if a dog farted in a room, and that stench were suppressed either by lozenges and incense, or by juniper wood: I ask you, does not the stench remain in the room just as much afterward as before? And although it may not be perceived by the sense of smell, is it therefore permitted for anyone to say the stench has been separated and no longer remains? On the contrary, it is present, but "corrected" by the fumigation. Thus the fumigation and the foul air enter the nostrils together. Of this kind also are the corrections of the Pharmacists, who blunt <term>Aleopaticum</term> <note>likely a reference to a bitter aloetic medicine</note> with sugar, so that it may inflict no harm. Thus sugar and honey are their <term>magisterium</term> <gloss>mastery</gloss>. Thus they also "correct" gentian with theriac. But are these not the works of donkey-like ignorance? Yet they boast and sell themselves as the Physicians of princes. But who is so stupid that he does not immediately smell that these things are worthless? What else, I ask, can they boast about their remedies, than to say: *This <term>Electuary</term> <gloss>a medicinal paste</gloss> is sweet, made of spices, sugar,*

<summary>Paracelsus argues that the true purpose of Alchemy in medicine is the separation of toxins from healing substances rather than the production of gold. He mocks contemporary pharmacists who merely mask the taste or effects of poisons with sugar instead of removing the harmful elements through fire and chemical separation.</summary>
<keywords>Alchemy, Toxicology, Separation, Pharmacology, Arcana, Diagridium, Purgatives, Medical Errors</keywords>
